verdict.summary: You can create a Google OAuth client and connect your own Gmail account in under an hour while the app is in Testing mode. Most useful Gmail scopes, including the https://mail.google.com/ scope in Composio's default set, are restricted. Opening the app to the public means Google verification plus a paid annual third-party security assessment (CASA), which takes weeks.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for Gates 1-2; several days of prep for verification and CASA (questionnaire, DAST scan, demo video, policies)
verdict.approval_wait: Several weeks for restricted scopes (Google's FAQ lists about 6 weeks; third parties report 2-8 weeks), plus the CASA assessment

gates.name: Testing (publishing status), developer as test user
gates.unlocks: You connect your own Google account through your own OAuth client and Composio custom auth config.
limits: Refresh tokens issued in Testing status expire after 7 days, so you have to reconnect weekly
Google shows an unverified-app warning for sensitive/restricted scopes

gates.name: Testing with test users (External), or Internal user type
gates.unlocks: Invited test users, or everyone in your Workspace/Cloud Identity org if you choose Internal, can connect without verification.
limits: External apps in Testing are capped at 100 test users (community-reported)
Test-user refresh tokens expire after 7 days
Internal user type needs a Workspace or Cloud Identity org. Plain @gmail.com accounts can't use it (community-reported). Internal apps avoid the 100-user cap and the 7-day expiry.
Unverified External apps set to In production reportedly have a lifetime cap of 100 new users, and each user sees the warning once

gates.name: In production + verified (restricted-scope verification)
gates.unlocks: Any Google user can connect. The 100-user cap, the 7-day token expiry and the unverified warning no longer apply.
limits: Every project that uses restricted scopes must be submitted for verification
Annual CASA security assessment by a Google-approved third party if restricted data passes through a third-party server (Composio's backend counts)
Brand verification is required for all apps
Refresh tokens generally don't expire unless revoked or unused for about 6 months
gates.time_to_reach: Several weeks (Google FAQ: about 6 weeks; third parties report 2-8 weeks) plus CASA scheduling

steps.title: Decide whether you need your own app
steps.detail: Composio's managed Gmail OAuth app works without any setup. Register your own only if you need your own consent-screen branding, custom scopes or a dedicated rate-limit quota. Toolkits without a custom auth config keep using managed auth.

steps.title: Sign in to Google Cloud Console and create a project
steps.detail: Sign in at console.cloud.google.com with the Google account that will own the app, then create (or pick) a Cloud project for this integration. Enable the Gmail API for the project in the API Library.
gotchas: The findings don't confirm whether a billing account or Workspace org is required to create the project.

steps.title: Configure the OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform)
steps.detail: Set the user type to External, or to Internal if every user is in your Workspace/Cloud Identity org. Leave the publishing status at Testing and add your own Google account as a test user.
gotchas: Internal isn't available to plain @gmail.com accounts.
Refresh tokens issued in Testing expire after 7 days.

steps.title: Pick the smallest set of Gmail scopes
steps.detail: Choose only the scopes your agent needs. In the scope picker, a lock icon means the scope is sensitive or restricted. gmail.send is reported as sensitive (verification but no CASA) and gmail.labels as non-sensitive. Most read/modify scopes and https://mail.google.com/ are restricted, which means verification plus CASA.
gotchas: Composio's default scope set includes https://mail.google.com/ (restricted). Drop it if gmail.send or narrower scopes are enough.
Sources disagree on some classifications. Check Google's Gmail API scopes page before deciding.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client ID
steps.detail: In Credentials, create an OAuth client ID of type Web application. Under Authorized redirect URIs, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. Copy the client ID and client secret.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The URI has to match character for character. Otherwise Google returns redirect_uri_mismatch.

steps.title: Create a custom Gmail auth config in Composio
steps.detail: Create a Gmail auth config with your client ID and secret, and put your chosen scopes in credentials.scopes (usually a comma-joined string). Make sure oauth_redirect_uri matches the URI you registered in Google. Pass the auth config ID in the session's authConfigs so Composio uses it instead of managed auth.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connected account from the auth config and finish Google consent with your test-user account. invalid_client means the client ID is wrong. redirect_uri_mismatch means the redirect URIs don't match.

steps.title: Add invited test users
steps.detail: Add each tester's Google account to the test-user list on the consent screen, up to the reported cap of 100. Warn testers about the unverified-app screen and the weekly reconnect forced by the 7-day expiry.

steps.title: Check whether an exemption applies
steps.detail: Google exempts personal use, development/testing/staging, service-owned data only, internal use within an organization, and domain-wide installation from restricted-scope verification. If you fit one of these, you may never need Gate 3. You also need to confirm your app is one of the allowed types in the Limited Use section.

steps.title: Prepare verification materials
steps.detail: Draft a privacy policy that covers secure data handling and deleting user data on request, a justification for each scope, and brand details for brand verification. Script a demo video. For a task-automation agent, the video must show how multiple API workflows are created and automated, and which directions user data flows.
gotchas: Google's exact list of required materials (homepage, domain verification, logo) wasn't fully extracted in the research. Check the console's verification checklist.

steps.title: Record the demo video and submit for verification
steps.detail: Record the demo video, switch the publishing status to In production, and submit the project for verification in the Google Auth Platform. Every project that uses restricted scopes must be submitted, and all OAuth clients in it that request restricted scopes must be ready.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: Book a Google-approved CASA lab and complete the assessment. Community reports describe a DAST scan, a 54-question questionnaire and encryption documentation. Reported cost is about $500-$4,500 per year (Tier 2 via TAC Security: $540-$1,800).

steps.title: Wait for Google's review
steps.detail: Restricted-scope verification can take several weeks. Google's FAQ lists about 6 weeks, and third parties report 2-8 weeks. Answer reviewer emails quickly to avoid delays.

steps.title: Renew CASA every year
steps.detail: The Letter of Validation is valid for 12 months, and the assessment has to be repeated each year to keep restricted-scope access.

requirements.item: Google account with access to Google Cloud Console
requirements.detail: The console requires a Google sign-in.
The redirect URI in Google must exactly match oauth_redirect_uri in the Composio auth config.
Up to 100 test users for External apps in Testing (community-reported).

requirements.item: Workspace/Cloud Identity org (Internal user type only)
requirements.detail: Needed only if you choose Internal instead of External.
The app must be one of the types allowed in the Limited Use section.
Task-automation platforms must show workflow creation and automation, and how user data flows.
Done by a Google-approved third party. Covers secure data handling and deleting user data on request. Reported cost: about $500-$4,500 per year.

scopes.effect: Full mailbox access. Included in Composio's default scope set. Needs restricted-scope verification plus annual CASA.

scopes.scope: gmail.readonly / gmail.modify / gmail.compose / gmail.insert / gmail.metadata / gmail.settings.basic / gmail.settings.sharing
scopes.effect: Restricted-scope verification plus CASA (third-party list; some sources disagree on gmail.readonly).
Needs OAuth verification but not the restricted-scope security assessment (third-party report).
Non-sensitive. No verification needed for this scope alone (third-party report).
Standard identity scopes listed in Google's OIDC discovery document.

blockers.cause: The redirect URI in the Google OAuth client doesn't exactly match the one in the Composio auth config.
blockers.fix: Copy the callback URL from your Composio auth config into Authorized redirect URIs exactly as shown.

blockers.symptom: invalid_client: The OAuth client was not found
blockers.cause: Wrong or deleted client ID in the auth config.
blockers.fix: Re-copy the client ID and secret from Google Credentials into Composio.

blockers.symptom: Users see a 'Google hasn't verified this app' warning
blockers.cause: Sensitive or restricted scopes are being requested before verification.
blockers.fix: Have testers click through during Gate 2, or remove unverified scopes from the request until Google verifies them.

blockers.symptom: Connections break about a week after authorizing
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens issued in Testing publishing status expire after 7 days.
blockers.fix: Reconnect, use the Internal user type if you have a Workspace org, or complete verification and move to production.

blockers.symptom: New users can't be added past 100
blockers.cause: The 100-user cap applies to unverified External apps.
CASA assessment missing, demo video incomplete, or app type not allowed under Limited Use.
blockers.fix: Complete CASA through an approved lab, record a video that shows the workflows and data flows, and confirm your app type is allowed.
blockers.contact: Google Auth Platform verification center in Cloud Console

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Gmail app for development. It needs no Google setup. Register your own Google OAuth client when you need your own consent-screen branding, custom or narrower scopes, or a dedicated quota. Set the client's authorized redirect URI to Composio's callback (https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback), create a custom Gmail auth config with the client ID, secret and credentials.scopes, and pass its ID in authConfigs. Composio's default scopes include the restricted https://mail.google.com/ scope. With your own app, that means Google verification plus CASA before public launch, so request narrower scopes if you can. The legacy redirect https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add is still supported.
